{"slug": "do-you-own-the-code-from-ai-website-builders", "title": "Do You Own the Code From AI Website Builders? (2026)", "metaTitle": "Do You Own the Code From AI Website Builders? (2026)", "metaDescription": "AI website builders do not all treat code ownership the same way. Here is how it varies across the category, and Kodely's honest, specific answer today.", "targetKeyword": "do you own the code from ai website builders", "category": "Glossary", "bodyHtml": "

Why this question matters

Every AI website builder gets you a working site in minutes. But the site does not really belong to you until you can answer a harder question: if you left the platform tomorrow, what would you actually be able to take with you? That is the lock-in question, and it matters for three practical reasons. First, migration - platforms change pricing, shut down, or stop suiting your needs, and you want the option to move. Second, trust - if a tool will not show you what it built, you cannot verify it, audit it, or learn from it. Third, leverage - knowing your exit options changes how you plan and grow on a platform, even if you never actually leave it.

How ownership varies across AI website builders

There is no single answer for the category, and anyone who tells you there is one is oversimplifying. Roughly, AI website builders fall into a few buckets:

  • Fully proprietary, non-portable builders. Some AI builders, like most drag-and-drop builders before them, render your site through their own proprietary system. There is no underlying React or HTML file you can point to and copy - what runs your site is configuration data that only their engine can interpret. Leave the platform and the site does not come with you in any usable form.
  • Code-generating tools with no export. Some newer AI builders genuinely generate real source files - components, markup, styles - and render them live. That is a meaningful step up: the code exists, in a real language, and you can often view it. But whether you can get the whole project out as a file you can run elsewhere depends entirely on whether the vendor has built an export feature yet.
  • Code-generating tools with full export. Others generate real code and also let you download or push the entire project, often to GitHub or as a zip, so you can self-host it, hand it to a developer, or migrate outright.

The difference between these buckets is architecture, not marketing copy. It is worth checking which bucket a tool is actually in before you build anything you would mind losing.

What owning the code actually requires

Ownership is really two separate capabilities that get blended together in marketing pages:

  • Visibility and access - can you see the real source files at all, at any time, without asking support or paying extra?
  • Full exportability - can you take the entire, working project out of the platform as a bundle you can run somewhere else?

A tool can have one without the other. You can be able to read and copy every file it writes and still have no one-click way to get the whole project out as a deployable package. That gap is exactly where most of the confusion in this category comes from, and it is worth being precise about instead of pretending it does not exist.

Kodely's position today, honestly

Kodely generates a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application - real component files, not a mockup and not markup only the platform can read. Every time Kodely builds or edits your site from a chat instruction, you can open the code view and see the actual generated source files, and copy any of them, at any time. Nothing is hidden or obfuscated.

What Kodely does not have yet is a one-click export of the whole project - no zip download, no push-to-GitHub button. If you want to take a specific component, page, or config file to use elsewhere, you can copy it right now. If you want to walk away with the entire working project in one action, that capability is not built yet.

So today, owning the code on Kodely means transparency and access, not yet full portability. We would rather say that plainly than let the phrase you own your code do work it has not earned. Full project export is a real gap, and it is on the roadmap, not a hidden feature.

What to ask before you commit to any AI builder

  • Is the output real code in a standard language and framework, or proprietary configuration only the platform can render?
  • Can you view and copy the source files today, for free, without contacting support?
  • Can you export the entire project as a bundle, and if not, is that on a near-term roadmap?
  • If you can export, does the code run standalone, or does it still depend on the platform's runtime or APIs?
  • What happens to your site and your data if you cancel or the company shuts down?

Ask these before you build anything you would be upset to lose. The answers tell you more about a platform than any feature list.

FAQ

Does Kodely let me download my whole project as a zip file?
Not yet. You can view and copy every generated source file individually inside the app. A full-project export is not available today.

Is the code Kodely generates real, or is it a proprietary format?
It is real: a Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application made of actual component files, rendered live in preview and visible in the in-app code view.

Can I move a Kodely site to another host?
Not as a one-click migration today. Publishing goes live on a name.kodely.site subdomain, and custom domains and full project export are not available yet.

Do other AI website builders let you export code?
It varies by tool. Some are fully proprietary and non-portable, some generate real code with no export, and some generate real code with full export options like GitHub push or zip download. Check which category a tool is in before relying on it.

What is the difference between viewing code and owning code?
Viewing and copying means you can see and reuse individual files right now. Owning, in the fullest sense, means you can take the entire working project with you in one action. They are related but not the same thing, and it is worth knowing which one a platform actually offers.

Want to see the real code Kodely generates for yourself? Build free and open the code view on your first project - no credit card required. You can also compare plans on pricing or read more on the blog.
